URL: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/22/russia-reports-injuries-after-top-online-retailer-wildberries-hit-again
Al Jazeera (newsroom), Wed 22 Jul 2026 09:30 GMT — Ukrainian drones again hit Wildberries (Russia's biggest online retailer) warehouses Wednesday, injuring eight. CEO Tatiana Kim: Krasnodar & Nevinnomyssk logistics centres evacuated. Stavropol governor Vladimir Vladimirov: warehouse fire near Nevinnomyssk, five treated. Krasnodar HQ: three more wounded by drone debris. Armavir: one worker killed by debris. (Saturday's Wildberries strike killed eight night-shift workers.)
Zelensky confirmed Wednesday's attacks: army targeted "important facilities in the Krasnodar and Stavropol regions" — "Logistics centres involved in supplying the Russian army with components for drones, navigation equipment and supplies, as well as another oil depot." "In the Black Sea and Azov Sea areas, a tanker and four cargo ships belonging to the Russian shadow fleet were hit... We are justly returning the war to its source – to Russia."
Unmanned Systems Forces cmdr Robert "Madyar" Brovdi: drones struck 13 Russian shadow-fleet vessels in Black/Azov seas in past 48h. AJ correspondent: part of Ukraine's "40-day influence operations" to "influence Russia back to the negotiating table." Outgoing C-in-C Oleksandr Syrskii: Ukraine recaptured 700 sq km this year. Russia claimed capture of Artilne (Kharkiv/Kupiansk) and Blahodatne (Zaporizhzhia); Kharkiv governor Syniehubov: 15 settlements attacked in 24h, 3 killed, 11 wounded.
